newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania to reopen schools under heavy guard.
newsitem.headline: Albania to reopen schools under heavy guard.

text.p: Schools and colleges of higher education, shut after an armed insurrection, will reopen under armed guard in the Albanian capital Tirana next week, the state news agency ATA said.

Schools throughout the small Balkan state were closed on March 2 under a state of emergency as Albanians, distraught over the loss of life savings in fraudulent savings schemes, plunged the country into violence. More than 300 people have been killed.
Education director Tomi Tomorri said the capital's secondary and primary schools and higher education colleges would reopen on April 29. It was not known when schools elsewhere would reopen.
School guards would be issued with arms and police officers would check schools, Tomorri said.
The government is struggling to restore order across the country as an Italian-led eight-nation force of 6,000 troops deploys to ensure food and medical supplies reach the needy.
In the latest incidents of violence, police were investigating the murders of a father and son, aged 60 and 40, found shot dead in the southern town of Permet on Thursday. The motive was not known.
Police released two prisoners from a police station in the industrial town of Elbasan after a gang of 20 masked men in central Albania shot at the building demanding their freedom, ATA said.
President Sali Berisha met representatives from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to prepare for general elections expected on June 29.

"Albania needs a strong government to come out of the forthcoming elections, that is a government with a solid parliamentary support which will be able to resolve the country's many complicated problems," Berisha said.
"I am making every effort to organise the elections as soon as possible," he added.
Greece delivered 42 tonnes of emergency food aid to Albania on Thursday, destined for destitute families and welfare institutions, the Greek embassy said.
